wifi_ap.title: Connect to your Wi-Fi · Step 1 of 3: pairing mode
wifi_ap.description:
Put the purifier in pairing mode:

1. Plug it in and switch it on.
2. Hold the **Wi-Fi** button for about **3 seconds**.
3. The appliance's Wi-Fi icon should **blink fast**: that means it is in pairing mode. If it does not, repeat the press.

In that mode the purifier creates its own Wi-Fi network, named like **AIR PURIFIER XXXX** (the last four characters differ from one appliance to another). Its password is on the appliance **label**.

wifi_tool.title: Connect to your Wi-Fi · Step 3 of 3: send your Wi-Fi to the purifier
wifi_tool.description:
With the computer **already connected to the purifier's network**, open the wizard that will send it your Wi-Fi. It guides you through its own screens, **needs no administrator rights** and sends nothing to the Internet.

**On Windows:** download **{exe_name}** from the [downloads page]({releases_url}) and open it (no installation needed). If Windows shows 'Windows protected your PC', click *More info → Run anyway*: the program is not signed.

**On macOS or Linux:** download [{tool_name}]({tool_url}) (right click → *Save link as…*) and run it with `python3 {tool_name}` (needs [Python 3](https://www.python.org/downloads/)).

The wizard checks that you are on the purifier's network and asks for your **Wi-Fi name and password**. Your Wi-Fi must be **2.4 GHz with WPA2 security** (mixed WPA2/WPA3 is fine) and **without Smart Connect** (one name for 2.4 and 5 GHz): in testing the purifier could not join with it enabled. At the end it **checks that the purifier shows up on your network** and shows its IP.

**How do I know it worked?** The purifier's Wi-Fi icon turns **solid** and the wizard says 'Done!'. If it blinks slowly and turns off, it could not join: check 2.4 GHz, WPA2 and Smart Connect, and start over from step 1.

When the wizard says 'Done!', come back here and press **Submit**.

wifi_connect.title: Connect to your Wi-Fi · Step 2 of 3: connect a computer to the purifier's network
wifi_connect.description:
Home Assistant cannot join the purifier's network, so you will use a **computer with Wi-Fi** (the same one on which you will open the wizard in the next step). Connect it to that network now:

1. From the computer's Wi-Fi icon, look for a network called **AIR PURIFIER** followed by four characters, for example **AIR PURIFIER XXXX**.
2. Connect using the password on the purifier's label.

- If the system warns that there is **no Internet**, that is normal: stay connected.
- If Windows jumps back to your home Wi-Fi, untick *Connect automatically* on that network while this runs.
- If you cannot see the network, check that the purifier's Wi-Fi icon is still blinking fast.

While the computer is on that network it will have no Internet; this is temporary.

data.allow_off_when_locked: Allow turning off while the panel is locked

data_description.allow_off_when_locked: Turning off over the network cancels the panel lock and it cannot be re-enabled over the network. When disabled, a warning is shown instead of turning off.

panel_locked.message: The purifier's panel is locked and turning it off over the network would remove the lock (it cannot be re-enabled over the network). Unlock it with the LOCK button, or allow turning off while locked in the integration options.
